source: Jagadish, Coda-Forno, Thalmann, Schulz, Binz (2024) Human-like category learning by injecting ecological priors from LLMs into neural networks
finding: A meta-learned model trained on category tasks written by Claude-v2 (ERMI) fits human category-learning choices better than seven cognitive models, including prototype (PM), exemplar (GCM), rule and rule-plus-exception (Rulex).
numbers: Lower BIC is better. Badham et al. 2017 data: ERMI BIC 38722.13 vs raw Claude-v2 prompting 39816.90. Devraj et al. 2021 data: ERMI 41207.20 vs Claude-v2 42401.42.
limits: Task generator is an LLM, but the fitted learner is a small meta-trained network, not the LLM. Claude-v2 is an old model.
agent_relevance: Classic prototype, exemplar and rule models were each beaten by a learner trained on realistic task statistics. For S0 problem classes, do not hard-code one strategy; choose by task statistics.

source: Jagadish, Coda-Forno, Thalmann, Schulz, Binz (2024) Human-like category learning by injecting ecological priors from LLMs into neural networks
finding: Raw Claude-v2 prompted as a learner did not reproduce the human order of Shepard-type difficulty and was a worse match to human error rates than ERMI.
numbers: Claude-v2 found type 2 tasks harder than types 3, 4 and 5 (humans do not). Mean squared error to human error rates: Claude-v2 0.18, ERMI 0.05.
limits: One model, one prompt format, 2023-era model.
agent_relevance: A plain prompted model should not be trusted to rank problem difficulty like a person. Use measured per-class pass rates instead.

source: Jagadish, Coda-Forno, Thalmann, Schulz, Binz (2024) Human-like category learning by injecting ecological priors from LLMs into neural networks
finding: Humans shift from prototype-like to exemplar-like categorisation with practice (Smith and Minda 1998 pattern). ERMI shows the shift; raw Claude-v2 is fully exemplar-based already after block 2.
numbers: ERMI trend over trial segments: -0.01 +/- 0.004 (z=-2.54, p<0.01). Humans better fit by prototype model for first five blocks. Claude-v2 exemplar-based from block 2 on Devraj et al. 2021 design.
quote: an LLM trained on the entire internet cannot explain human category learning
limits: Strategy labels come from fitting PM and GCM to choices; the fit is model-dependent.
agent_relevance: An in-context LLM learner seems to store and compare instances from the start. Early-trial advice (few examples) may favour the abstract rule rather than similarity to instances.

source: Jagadish, Coda-Forno, Thalmann, Schulz, Binz (2024) Human-like category learning by injecting ecological priors from LLMs into neural networks
finding: Training on LLM-generated task statistics also gave strong tabular classification: ERMI beat tuned baselines on OpenML-CC18.
numbers: Reported as state of the art on the OpenML-CC18 benchmark (see paper table for per-dataset numbers).
limits: Not re-checked per dataset here.
agent_relevance: Shows LLM-written tasks can serve as a prior source; a source of problem classes for a gate.

source: Jagadish, Thalmann, Coda-Forno, Binz, Schulz (2026 v3) Meta-learning ecological priors from LLMs explains human learning and decision making
finding: Extended ERMI to 15 experiments across function learning, category learning and decision making; still beats established cognitive models on trial-by-trial prediction and keeps the prototype-to-exemplar shift.
numbers: 15 experiments. Category models compared: RMC, prototype (PM), exemplar (GCM), rule. Humans early blocks prototype-better, later blocks exemplar-better; ERMI starts indistinguishable then turns exemplar-based.
limits: Preprint, simulated tasks from LLM; human data are earlier published studies.
agent_relevance: Supports 'strategy depends on experience and task statistics' as a design principle for choosing a method per problem.

source: Chan, Dasgupta, Kim, Kumaran, Lampinen, Hill (2022) Transformers generalize differently from information stored in context vs weights
finding: Transformers trained from scratch on controlled stimuli generalise from weights by rule but from context by exemplar (nearest-example comparison). Pretraining on sequences that require rules can overcome the in-context exemplar bias.
numbers: Held-out combination BX: in-context models picked the label of AX or BW about equally (totally exemplar-based). In-weights generalisation fully rule-based.
limits: Small synthetic transformers, two-feature stimuli.
agent_relevance: What you put in the prompt is used by exemplar similarity unless the model has a rule-like prior. Stating the rule explicitly may be needed.

source: Chan, Dasgupta, Kim, Kumaran, Lampinen, Hill (2022) Transformers generalize differently from information stored in context vs weights
finding: A 70B pretrained language model, tested on shape and colour words with nonsense labels, generalised from context in a significantly rule-based way, and more so at larger size.
numbers: Sizes 1B, 7B, 70B. 1B model was effectively exact exemplar-based; rule-ness grew with scale. The 70B model preferred generalising along colour over shape in the control condition.
quote: in-context learning is significantly rule-based, with larger models showing more rule-basedness
limits: One model family (Chinchilla-type), simple 2-feature task; scale effect not seen in from-scratch synthetic models.
agent_relevance: Larger models behave more like rule learners in-context; small or cheap models used inside the loop will lean on surface similarity.

source: Dasgupta, Grant, Griffiths (2022) Distinguishing rule- and exemplar-based generalization in learning systems
finding: Protocol from category-learning psychology (cue conflict, zero-shot, partial exposure) that separates feature bias from exemplar-versus-rule bias in ML systems. Standard networks come out feature-biased and exemplar-based.
numbers: Exemplar-vs-rule score EvR: LSTM on sentiment text EvR=0.54 (partial-exposure accuracy fell to 30.1% from 84% zero-shot). ResNets on CelebA show positive EvR even with no feature bias; no change across ResNet widths and depths.
limits: Not LLM prompting; trained networks. Binary tasks with a distractor feature.
agent_relevance: A cheap test for our agent: give it a task where a distractor feature is shortcut-correlated and check if it follows a rule or matches instances.

source: Van Maldegem, van de Ven, Op de Beeck, Tuytelaars (2025) Replicating Posner and Keele (1968) with standard convolutional neural networks
finding: Three CNNs (AlexNet, DenseNet-121, ResNet-18) trained on Posner and Keele Experiment III dot patterns did not match human results. AlexNet and DenseNet-121 classified the unseen prototype better than new exemplars: a weak prototype effect.
numbers: Six classes of 9-dot patterns, 4 training exemplars at 7.7-bit distortion; errors to criterion: humans 37.5, AlexNet 34.72, DenseNet-121 9.59, ResNet-18 6.52.
limits: Conference abstract, vision models, not LLMs; no day-2 test.
agent_relevance: Prototype effects in machines are weak and architecture-dependent; do not assume a prototype extraction from examples happens by default.

source: Xiong, Ji-An, Wilson, Lee, Wei (2026) Large language models reorganize representational geometry during in-context learning
finding: On binary labels defined by projecting an LLM's own representations on axes, in-context learnability varies by axis even though all tasks are linearly separable. Successful learning comes with better class separability in the final layer.
numbers: Eight LLMs on ETHICS-commonsense; Qwen3-4B across five datasets. Amplifying activity along the task axis did not improve behaviour.
limits: Descriptive fit of behaviour, not proof the model runs a prototype algorithm (authors say so).
agent_relevance: What can be learned from examples is limited by the model's existing representation geometry. Few-shot examples will not teach a distinction the model does not already represent.

source: Xiong, Ji-An, Wilson, Lee, Wei (2026) Large language models reorganize representational geometry during in-context learning
finding: Of six online learners (prototype, exemplar, 1-NN, online gradient descent, Bayesian class mean, Kalman filter) run on the LLM's final-layer states, the prototype learner best predicted the LLM's trial-by-trial answers.
numbers: Prototype best across eight LLMs and across five datasets; more flexible linear learners reached higher task accuracy from the same representations.
quote: LLM behavior is best described by a prototype-like algorithm
limits: Fit is to behaviour, on binary tasks; contrasts with Chan 2022 where exemplar behaviour was seen in small trained transformers.
agent_relevance: In-context learning in LLMs can look like centroid averaging: noisy or off-centre examples may be averaged away. Choose representative examples.

source: Fu, Cho, Lee, Kim (2026) LLMs learn better in-context from rules than from examples
finding: Across five tasks (Set Game, Tapatan, Operator Function, Noun Class Agreement, Lexical Category Inference) models learned more reliably from a written rule than from input-output examples. Adding examples to the rule gave no significant gain.
numbers: Gemma 3, Qwen 2.5, Qwen 3 and other base and instruction-tuned models, 7B to 32B. Rule-minus-example gap largest on Operator Function and Set Game (about +0.3 to +0.4 accuracy). Combined rules+examples tracked rules alone.
limits: Open models only; demonstrations chosen for minimum coverage, not optimised; authors note it may limit example gains.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for the rule-first side: when a rule can be stated, send the rule. Examples add little on top.

source: Fu, Cho, Lee, Kim (2026) LLMs learn better in-context from rules than from examples
finding: Instruction tuning raised rule-based learning but not example-based learning. The rule advantage shrinks where the task needs distributional cues or stored world knowledge.
numbers: Instruct minus base: +0.178 accuracy for rules, -0.024 for examples. Larger models (14-32B) beat small (7-12B): +0.213 for base and +0.063 for instruct (as read from the figure). Rule gain small for Tapatan, Noun Class Agreement and Lexical Category Inference.
limits: Exact per-condition values read from figure labels; check the paper tables before quoting.
agent_relevance: Task-type routing: algebraic or rule tasks get rules; semantic category tasks gain less from rules.

source: Fu, Cho, Lee, Kim (2026) LLMs learn better in-context from rules than from examples
finding: In Lexical Category Inference, example-based learning was better for conjunctive (AND) than disjunctive (OR) category definitions, as in human studies (Bruner et al. 1956). This split did not show consistently under rule-based or combined prompts.
numbers: Sequence-judgment task with semantic categories such as birds AND lives in South America. See paper Appendix D, Tables 6-7, for AND minus OR gaps (one reads +10.7 points).
limits: Appendix values only partly read.
agent_relevance: Disjunctive classes (several unlike subtypes) are a known weak spot when learning from examples; rules help there.

source: Wang, McCoy, Steinert-Threlkeld (2024) Minimization of Boolean complexity in in-context concept learning
finding: In-context concept learning accuracy falls as the minimal description length of the concept grows, a simplicity bias like the human result of Feldman (2000).
numbers: 18 concepts per complexity class 1-5. Gemma-2-9B 83% to 66%; Qwen2-72B 90% to 74%. Pearson r with complexity: Gemma-2-9B -0.961 (p=0.009), Gemma-2-27B -0.898 (p=0.038), Qwen2-7B -0.884 (p=0.046), Qwen2-72B -0.854 (p=0.065).
limits: Only 5 class means per model, so the r values rest on 5 points. Numerical concepts only, 4 models.
agent_relevance: Concept difficulty can be estimated by rule length; use this as a prior for how much search budget a classification-style problem needs.

source: Qiu, Jiang, Lu, et al. (2024) Phenomenal yet puzzling: testing inductive reasoning of language models with hypothesis refinement
finding: Rule-induction loop (propose, select, refine textual rules) with a symbolic interpreter beats plain input-output prompting on rule-learning tasks (ACRE, MiniSCAN, List Functions). The model proposes good rules but cannot apply them reliably.
numbers: Raw accuracy, IO vs best refinement: ACRE 64.0 vs 79.8 (T=1,N=5); MiniSCAN 61.7 vs 77.0 (T=3,N=1). Task accuracy ACRE 28.0 vs 48.0; MiniSCAN 0.0 vs 46.0. MiniARC raw fell: 33.1 IO vs 12.8.
limits: The gain depends on an external symbolic interpreter; MiniARC lost, likely because it needs pattern matching.
agent_relevance: This is the rule-category loop an agent can run: propose rules, check by code, revise on real failures (fits G2, G3).

source: Qiu, Jiang, Lu, et al. (2024) Phenomenal yet puzzling: testing inductive reasoning of language models with hypothesis refinement
finding: Applying its own rule is where the model fails. With the model itself as interpreter instead of code, accuracy collapses on some tasks.
numbers: Task accuracy with symbolic vs LM interpreter: MiniSCAN over 80% to about 0%; ACRE 59.0 symbolic vs 47.0 LM (figure labels).
limits: Figure values partly read from layout text.
agent_relevance: A rule written by the model must be executed by code, not by the model. Directly supports the program-decides split.

source: Qiu, Jiang, Lu, et al. (2024) Phenomenal yet puzzling: testing inductive reasoning of language models with hypothesis refinement
finding: Language models are brittle to noisy examples in rule induction. Human comparison on the same tasks gives about 80% average for ACRE-like tasks and 45.9% for List Functions.
numbers: Noise levels tested: 12.5%, 25%, 50% of examples perturbed. Human averages from prior work listed in Appendix C: about 80% (ACRE), 45.9% (List Functions), 90.9% (ConceptARC).
limits: Human baselines come from other papers, not run in the same session.
agent_relevance: Check examples for noise before trusting an induced rule; one wrong example can break a rule fit to every example.

source: Russin, Pavlick, Frank (2025) The dynamic interplay between in-context and in-weight learning in humans and neural networks
finding: Llama 2 and GPT-3.5 learned a rule-like colour-animal composition task from 9 in-context examples far better than a rotated (information-integration style) version. Blocked order helped Llama 2 on the rule-like task.
numbers: Llama 2 rule-like blocked 601/640 (93.9%), rule-like interleaved 478/576 (83.0%), rotated blocked 23.6%, rotated interleaved 24.5%. GPT-3.5 showed no significant order effect (p=0.63). Rotation chi2=428.6, p<2.2e-16.
limits: Two models; table partly garbled in extraction, values recomputed from counts.
agent_relevance: In-context learning is rule-friendly and poor on non-axis-aligned boundaries. Present rule-like problems in blocked, grouped order.

source: Xu, Zhang, Du, Luo, Qiu, Huang, Zhang (2025) Revealing emergent human-like conceptual representations from language prediction (PNAS)
finding: Representations that LLaMA-style models build in context support both prototype and exemplar categorisation of THINGS categories, with prototype slightly ahead.
numbers: Prototype: 90.87% (+/-0.25) with 48 demonstrations on THINGSplus, 92.37% (+/-0.13) on original THINGS. Exemplar (nearest neighbour): 87.46% and 88.63%. With 24 demonstrations: 90.64% (FastText 77.86%, sense vectors 85.13%).
limits: Accuracy of a readout on embeddings, not model answers to a prompt.
agent_relevance: Category membership of ordinary objects is well encoded; the category step is rarely the weak point for natural concepts.

source: Pedrotti et al. (2025) How humans and LLMs organize conceptual knowledge: subordinate categories in Italian (ACL)
finding: On exemplar generation, category induction and typicality, LLM alignment with Italian speakers is low for subordinate categories, and highest for encyclopedic categories.
numbers: Valid exemplars: LLaMA-3.1-70B about 82%, Mistral-7B 52%, LLaVA-7B 44%. Overlap with human exemplars about 24-29% overall (12% FURNISHING). Typicality accuracy LLaMA-3.1-70B 73% in low-productivity setting.
limits: Italian, perplexity-based probes, categories from one lab's norms.
agent_relevance: Typicality and prototype-style structure from text is partial; do not use model typicality as ground truth for a class label.

source: Zhao, Zhu, Lin, et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: An agent that keeps both abstracted insights (rule-like) and retrieved past trajectories (exemplar-like) beats either alone. Which one matters more depends on the task.
numbers: Insights-only vs retrieval-only success: HotpotQA 36% vs 31%; ALFWorld 50% vs 55%; WebShop 37% vs 38%. ExpeL matched Reflexion on HotpotQA (40% at R3 vs 39%).
limits: GPT-4 for insight extraction; three benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Direct agent-loop version of the rule-versus-exemplar split: knowledge tasks favour distilled rules, action-sequence tasks favour recalled instances. Keep both stores.

source: Allard, Teinturier, Xing, Viaud (2026) Experiential reflective learning for self-improving LLM agents
finding: Distilled heuristics from single attempts beat raw trajectories used as few-shot examples on Gaia2. Selective retrieval beats stuffing everything.
numbers: Overall success 56.1% for the method, +7.8 points over ReAct baseline (about 48.3). Few-shot trajectories about 46.4 in the bar chart (below baseline). Random heuristics peak near 40-60 then decline; best random 53.8%; embedding retrieval 53.3%; failure-only 58.9% overall but weak on Execution (47.6).
limits: Workshop paper, 3 runs, one benchmark; bar-chart labels read from layout text.
agent_relevance: Agrees with Fu 2026: abstracted rules transfer better than raw instances. Supports retrieval on a signal, not on a schedule.

source: Feldman (2000) Minimization of Boolean complexity in human concept learning (Nature)
finding: Human ease of learning Boolean concepts falls with the length of the shortest logical formula.
numbers: Cited in Wang 2024 as strong negative correlation; figures not read.
limits: Not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Human benchmark for the simplicity bias in LLMs.

source: Davidson et al. (2026) function vectors under rules versus examples, cited in Fu 2026
finding: Cited in Fu 2026: rule and example prompts for the same task activate only partly overlapping internal mechanisms, not one shared function vector.
numbers: not read
limits: Second-hand via Fu 2026; title and venue not verified.
agent_relevance: Supports using both formats, but Fu 2026 finds no additive gain.

source: Liu et al. (2024) cited in Fu 2026: rule-based learning outperforms example-based when rules are correct
finding: Earlier finding that rule prompts beat example prompts when the stated rule is correct.
numbers: not read
limits: Second-hand; condition is that the rule is correct.
agent_relevance: Wrong rules are the risk; check rules by code.

source: Singh et al. (2021) CNN prototype effect, cited in Van Maldegem 2025
finding: Earlier test of whether networks show a human prototype effect, cited as the prior study.
numbers: not read
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: Prior art on prototype effects in machines.
